title: 1985 AHSME Problem 11
statement: How many distinguishable rearrangements of the letters in CONTEST have both the vowels first? (For instance, OETCNST is one such arrangement, but OTETSNC is not.)

solutions.text:
The vowels \(O,E\) can be ordered first in \(2!\) ways. The remaining letters \(C,N,T,S,T\) can be arranged in \(\frac{5!}{2!}=60\) distinguishable ways because the two \(T\)’s agree. The total is \(2\cdot60=120.\)

Thus the correct answer is B.
hints: Order the two vowels in the first two positions
Permute the remaining five letters while accounting for the repeated \(T\)
